text: The device hums. Evening, outside a town far to the north, near Haran. Ten camels kneel by a well, dusty from a long road.
Abraham is old now, and Sarah has died. Abraham has sent his chief servant back to his own relatives, to find a wife for Isaac.
As evening approached, he made the camels kneel down near the well outside the town at the time when the women went out to draw water.

speaker: Abraham's servant
text: A long, long road from the Negev, {name}.

speaker: Abraham's servant
text: A friendly face! I have to find the right wife for my master's son, and I do not even know where to start. I will ask the LORD.

speaker: Abraham's servant
text: O LORD, God of my master Abraham, | please grant me success today, and show kindness to my master Abraham. Here I am, standing beside the spring, and the daughters of the townspeople are coming out to draw water. Now may it happen that the girl to whom I say, ‘Please let down your jar that I may drink,’ and who responds, ‘Drink, and I will water your camels as well’—let her be the one You have appointed for Your servant Isaac. By this I will know that You have shown kindness to my master.
Before the servant had finished praying, Rebekah came out with her jar on her shoulder. She was the daughter of Bethuel son of Milcah, the wife of Abraham’s brother Nahor.
… She went down to the spring, filled her jar, and came up again.
God was already answering before the prayer was even finished.

speaker: Abraham's servant
text: Please let me have a little water from your jar.

speaker: Rebekah
text: Drink, my lord,
… and she quickly lowered her jar to her hands and gave him a drink.

speaker: Rebekah
text: I will also draw water for your camels, until they have had enough to drink.
Ten thirsty camels after a long journey. Rebekah offered to water them all without being asked.

speaker: Abraham's servant
text: Help her, {name}! Fill a jar at the well and pour it into the trough.
A deep well, with a bucket on a rope.
You lower the bucket and fill your jar. Now pour it into the trough.
Your jar is full. Pour it into the trough.
A long stone trough for the animals.
Fill a jar at the well first.
Splash! The camels crowd in to drink, and Rebekah runs past with another jar.

speaker: Rebekah
text: More water! They're so thirsty.

And she quickly emptied her jar into the trough and ran back to the well to draw water, until she had drawn water for all his camels. Meanwhile, the man watched her silently to see whether or not the LORD had made his journey a success.
And after the camels had finished drinking, he took out a gold ring weighing a beka, and two gold bracelets for her wrists weighing ten shekels.

speaker: Abraham's servant
text: Whose daughter are you? | Please tell me, is there room in your father’s house for us to spend the night?

speaker: Rebekah
text: I am the daughter of Bethuel, the son that Milcah bore to Nahor. | We have plenty of straw and feed, as well as a place for you to spend the night.
Then the man bowed down and worshiped the LORD,

speaker: Abraham's servant
text: Blessed be the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who has not withheld His kindness and faithfulness from my master. As for me, the LORD has led me on the journey to the house of my master’s relatives.
The servant asked God for help, watched for His answer, and then stopped to thank Him.
The girl ran and told her mother’s household about these things. Now Rebekah had a brother named Laban, and he rushed out to the man at the spring.

speaker: Laban
text: Come, you who are blessed by the LORD, | Why are you standing out here? I have prepared the house and a place for the camels.

speaker: Laban
text: Come in, come in! Everything is ready.
Inside, before he will eat a bite, the servant tells the whole story: Abraham, his prayer at the well, and Rebekah and the camels.

speaker: Laban and Bethuel
text: This is from the LORD; we have no choice in the matter. Rebekah is here before you. Take her and go, and let her become the wife of your master’s son, just as the LORD has decreed.
The next morning the servant wants to leave at once. Her family would like her to stay ten days more, so they ask Rebekah.
They called Rebekah and asked her, “Will you go with this man?” “I will go,” she replied.
Like Abraham long before, Rebekah left her home for a land she had never seen, trusting God.

speaker: Rebekah
text: I have never been so far from home. But I am sure, {name}.
Then Rebekah and her servant girls got ready, mounted the camels, and followed the man. So the servant took Rebekah and left.
Day after day the camels sway south, back along the long road Abraham once took.
Now Isaac had just returned from Beer-lahai-roi, for he was living in the Negev. Early in the evening, Isaac went out to the field to meditate, and looking up, he saw the camels approaching.

speaker: Rebekah
text: Who is that man in the field coming to meet us?

speaker: Abraham's servant
text: It is my master,
And when Rebekah looked up and saw Isaac, she got down from her camel …
Then the servant told Isaac all that he had done. And Isaac brought her into the tent of his mother Sarah and took Rebekah as his wife. And Isaac loved her and was comforted after his mother’s death.
A servant's prayer, a girl's kindness, and God leading every step. Through Isaac and Rebekah, God's promise to Abraham goes on.
Your device hums. Time to go.

speaker: Camel driver
text: Before we left, our master Abraham said something I keep thinking about.
… He will send His angel before you so that you can take a wife for my son from there.

speaker: Girl at the well
text: She's watering all ten camels? Do you know how much a thirsty camel drinks?
A thirsty camel can drink more than 25 gallons (about 100 liters) at once. Watering ten would take many, many trips with a jar.
Long after, Jesus taught His followers to do more than they are asked:

speaker: Jesus
text: … if someone forces you to go one mile, go with him two miles.

speaker: Rebekah's mother
text: My daughter, going so far away! We have a blessing for her to take with her.
And they blessed Rebekah and said to her, “Our sister, may you become the mother of thousands upon thousands. …

speaker: Rebekah's nurse
text: I have looked after her since she was a baby. Did you think I would let her go all this way alone?
So they sent their sister Rebekah on her way, along with her nurse and Abraham’s servant and his men.
Her name was Deborah. When she died, many years later, she was buried under an oak near Bethel, and Rebekah's son Jacob named the place (Genesis 35:8).

The servant prayed, then watched for God's answer. God leads people who ask Him, often through ordinary kindness, like a drink of water.
Abraham sent his chief servant to his relatives far to the north, to find a wife for Isaac. (24:1-10)
At the well the servant prayed for a sign. Before he finished, Rebekah came, gave him a drink and watered all ten camels. (24:11-21)
The servant thanked God for leading him to Abraham's relatives. Her family agreed: "This is from the LORD." (24:22-51)
Asked "Will you go with this man?", Rebekah said, "I will go." In the Negev she met Isaac, and he loved her. (24:52-67)
